intro: Multiplying many small feature likelihoods can erase a useful class comparison. Work with their logarithms instead.
task: Return class log-joint scores and predicted classes from supplied Gaussian naive Bayes parameters.
requirements: X is a nonempty finite (n,d) matrix; means and variances have shape (classes,d). Priors is a positive vector summing to one within 1e-7.
Every variance is strictly positive. Use the conditional-independence Gaussian likelihood, including its normalizing constant.
Return log_joint as an (n,classes) NumPy array and predictions as a NumPy integer vector. Ties choose the first class.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Broadcast observations against class means to obtain an (n,classes,d) array.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Include log(2π variance), not just the squared deviation term.

explanation: Naive Bayes assumes features are conditionally independent given the class. That assumption turns a joint likelihood into a product of individual densities.
Logarithms turn the product into a sum. Adding log priors produces log-joint scores; normalizing them into probabilities is unnecessary for choosing the largest score.

Hold the feature parameters equal and change the priors. Then hold priors equal and change a variance. Explain why a broad Gaussian can be less confident near its mean but assign more density far away.
formula: log p(c,x) = log πc − ½Σj [log(2πσ²cj) + (xj − μcj)²/σ²cj]
